stories.head: Somantra Launches Brand Engagement Score for AEO and GEO Across ChatGPT, Google AI, Claude and Perplexity
stories.plain: Somantra introduces a new metric that scores how deeply AI search engines elaborate on a brand across multi-turn conversations, benchmarked against competitors named in the same answer. This matters because marketers now need a measurable way to track brand visibility inside AI-generated answers — not just traditional search rankings — turning GEO from a concept into a trackable KPI.

stories.head: OtterlyAI Launches Agent Analytics to Make AI Crawler Traffic and AI Search ROI Measurable
stories.plain: OtterlyAI reads server logs to show marketers every AI agent and crawler visiting their site, then connects that crawl activity to visibility in AI answers. This is a practical first step toward end-to-end AI search ROI attribution — a gap that has blocked serious GEO budget decisions since AI answer engines emerged.

stories.head: InMobi Advertising Launches Conversational AI Agent for Media Buyers on Self-Serve Buyer Hub
stories.plain: InMobi's new conversational AI agent lets media buyers discover and transact premium ad inventory through natural language on its self-serve platform. This shifts programmatic buying from form-based UIs to agent-driven deal-making, a meaningful workflow change for how agencies access and negotiate inventory at scale.

stories.head: The Data Trust Crisis: Why Customer Data Quality Is Deteriorating and What to Do About It
stories.plain: Customer data is decaying faster than most teams realize, quietly undermining personalization and AI-driven decisions. The piece argues for a high-trust measurement framework built around data quality governance — a foundational issue that affects every AI system downstream, from CDPs to agentic campaigns.

stories.head: Iyuno Details Multi-Agent Architecture Behind CLOE for Consistent AI Content Production at Scale
stories.plain: Iyuno explains how its multi-agent system CLOE maintains continuity across scenes, episodes, and languages — solving the real production problem of AI-generated content losing consistency at scale. The architectural detail matters for teams evaluating whether agentic content pipelines can replace or augment human editorial workflows.

stories.head: OpenAI adds product carousels and AppsFlyer attribution to compete for ad dollars
stories.plain: ChatGPT is adding product carousels and performance attribution via AppsFlyer, moving it from an experimental ad channel to one performance marketers can measure and optimize. This reshapes how brands must think about discovery budgets and where AI-generated answers sit in the purchase funnel.

stories.head: Liferay report: only 24% of companies have a company-wide AI usage policy as agentic adoption accelerates
stories.plain: A 2026 survey finds most companies are deploying AI agents faster than they are writing rules to govern them — only 24% have a company-wide AI policy and just 25% track impact with clear KPIs. For MarTech buyers, this is a concrete signal that governance infrastructure is now a procurement requirement, not an afterthought.

stories.head: AI debt: every capability marketing gains with AI creates hidden governance and integration work
stories.plain: Faster content and campaign production with AI quietly accumulates technical and operational debt — ungoverned prompts, unmeasured outputs, and integrations nobody owns. The article gives marketing ops leaders a framework to identify where that debt is building before it becomes a liability.

stories.head: OtterlyAI launches Agent Analytics to make AI crawler traffic and GEO ROI measurable
stories.plain: OtterlyAI now reads server logs to show marketers which AI agents and crawlers are visiting their site and links that crawl activity to visibility inside AI-generated answers. It is one of the first tools to connect GEO effort to measurable ROI, filling a gap that has made AI search spending hard to justify.

stories.head: Somantra launches Brand Engagement Score to measure how deeply AI search answers elaborate on a brand
stories.plain: Somantra introduces a new metric that scores how substantively ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Claude, and Perplexity elaborate on a brand across multi-turn buyer conversations, benchmarked against competitors named in the same answer. This gives marketers a standardized way to track and improve brand presence inside AI-generated responses.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Are Replacing Whole Tool Categories, Not Just Features
body: The shift from AI augmenting existing martech to AI supplanting entire categories is no longer hypothetical. Conversational agents for media buying, CRM-native learning systems, and multi-agent content workflows signal that point solutions built around a single workflow are being absorbed into orchestration layers.

This matters for procurement decisions today: tools you renew this quarter may face category-level obsolescence within a planning cycle. Liferay's governance research underlines that speed of agent adoption is outpacing the guardrails organisations have in place, making architecture choices — not feature comparisons — the real differentiator.

themes.head: Brand Visibility Now Requires AI-Search Measurement
body: When ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews become the first touchpoint in product discovery, standard SEO metrics go blind. New instruments like Somantra's Brand Engagement Score and OtterlyAI's Agent Analytics are emerging specifically to measure how AI engines cite and surface brands — a metric category that did not exist 18 months ago.

Marketers who wait for these signals to mature risk operating on stale data while their share-of-AI-voice erodes. The broader piece on how AI, publishers, and social are rewriting product discovery confirms that the funnel entry point has structurally shifted, demanding a parallel measurement infrastructure alongside legacy analytics.

themes.head: The Data Trust Crisis Is Quietly Rotting Every AI Model
body: AI outputs are only as reliable as the customer data fed into them, and that data is actively degrading. Identity fragmentation, consent fatigue, and incomplete CRM hygiene mean that the foundation most AI marketing stacks are built on is cracking — an issue compounded by the AI debt accumulated when teams automate workflows before auditing the underlying data.

Two concurrent pieces — on AI debt hidden in faster marketing and on the 2027 CMO planning challenge — frame this as a strategic liability, not a technical footnote. Leaders who ignore data quality while scaling AI-generated content or personalisation will amplify errors at production speed rather than catching them.
ev: MarTech · AI debt in faster marketing

themes.head: Human Judgment Becomes the Scarce Premium Input in AI Creative
body: As generative AI handles execution, the skills commanding a premium are shifting toward those machines cannot replicate: nuanced judgment, strategic framing, and verification. The Agile Brand expert-mode piece argues explicitly that efficiency is no longer the differentiator — the human capacity to contextualise and challenge AI outputs is. MarTech's skills piece reinforces this, identifying critical thinking and prompt governance as the roles AI is making more valuable, not redundant.

The practical implication is a talent and workflow redesign question, not just a tools question. The observation that verification cannot be delegated runs through multiple threads this month, suggesting that any organisation treating AI as a fully autonomous creative layer is taking on unacknowledged reputational risk.

themes.head: AI Platforms Are Entering the Ad Market as Competitors, Not Tools
body: OpenAI adding advertising technology is a category-boundary event: the same AI layer that powers many marketers' workflows is now competing directly for ad budgets. Combined with AI-native product discovery reshaping where consumers first encounter brands, the traditional walled-garden ad ecosystem faces structural pressure from an entirely new class of intermediary.

For media planners, this is not a distant scenario — it requires scenario-planning ad-mix strategies today that account for AI platforms as both distribution channels and budget competitors. The prompt-governance and cost-management conversation that emerged this month is an early signal that teams are beginning to treat AI infrastructure spending with the same scrutiny once reserved for paid media.

month.takeaway: Every major decision in marketing technology right now — what to measure, what to build, where to spend, who to hire — is being forced to reset because AI has moved from a feature layer to a structural layer that is simultaneously replacing tools, reshaping discovery, degrading data, and entering the ad market as a competitor.
